# Objective

- Fixes #12411 
- Add an example demonstrating the usage of asset meta files.

## Solution

- Add a new example displaying a basic scene of three pixelated images
- Apply a .meta file to one of the assets setting Nearest filtering
- Use AssetServer::load_with_settings on the last one as another way to achieve the same effect
- The result is one blurry image and two crisp images demonstrating a common scenario in which changing settings are useful.

issue_context.title: Asset Meta Files should have an example
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

Asset Meta Files were introduced in [0.12](https://bevyengine.org/news/bevy-0-12/#asset-meta-files) but do not have an example in the repository.

This was inspired by a [discord help question](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/1216248019310346280/1216248019310346280) asking simply how to change texture filtering for a specific asset. Without meta files the answer to this is not simple. The docs for [`AssetLoader`](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/asset/trait.AssetLoader.html) and [`ImageLoader`](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/render/texture/struct.ImageLoader.html) do not provide straightforward guidance for users looking to utilize meta files.

An example in the repo would help users use meta files for simple tasks like changing texture filtering. Texture filtering would make a good example case, in my opinion.
